english_verification.review_scope: Checked the current Mod's F27 identity, opening vassals by the recorded representative mission/history scope, English naming, the Queendom Claim transition, F98 formation event, and fixed-revision Harpy background pages; not a full mission reward or formation audit. Native English national-idea names and descriptions were compared by localisation key by the primary. Large source intervals are locator envelopes, not a claim to inspect every intervening line or establish complete runtime reachability.
unresolved: The Ayarallen Queendom page preserves older naming and does not establish that current F27 is already F98.
Wiki background on roosts does not certify current mission effects, power costs, or the year of formation.
Current Mod cp1252 history gives Ištara I Ayarato; the Wiki infobox gives Ištara I Arayato. This is a source spelling difference, not a newly discovered ruler.

rationale.campaign_length: F27 has 20 direct missions, followed by Harpylen's independent long campaign after formation.
rationale.colonization: The dedicated prequel focuses on Bulwar integration rather than colonisation.
rationale.complexity: Two vassals, diplomatic relations, nest construction, de-monsterisation, and the formation gate run in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: There are old raids, conquest, and strong rule, but also explicit routes toward reconciliation, coexistence, and governance.
rationale.difficulty: The challenge comes more from multi-track management and the late formation gate than from weak opening forces.
rationale.diplomacy: Two opening vassals, loyalty and marriage, neighbouring relations, and multi-peoples arrangements form the core loop.
rationale.early_pressure: Existing vassals and a powerful ruler ease the opening pressure, but integration, relations, and regional rivals require management.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The opening ruler is magically capable and the F98 successor has a stronger magic line; the F27 prequel is not a pure spellcasting loop.
rationale.narrative_density: The old Queendom, sister tribes, human-goblin coexistence, and proclamation of the Fourth Queendom form one prequel.
rationale.tall_play: Nests, roads, workshops, universities, and valley cities are mission requirements.
rationale.trade_economy: Cities, roads, and external trade supply the multi-peoples Queendom.
rationale.warfare: Unifying the hills and expanding through Bulwar require war, but many steps can use vassals and diplomacy.

identity.appearance: An existing Firanyan Harpy matrilineal country in 1444; Nanšalen (F80) and Hytiranyalen (F81) begin as vassals.

successors.relationship: The F27 finale calls the formation effect, changes the Tag, and switches to F98's dedicated missions; other qualifying Harpy countries can also form F98.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
The first harpy state to appear in Bulwar was established all the way back in 1159 BA by the first Harpy Queen, Firanya. It quickly became one of the dominant forces in Bulwar, controlling much of Northern Bulwar and establishing tributaries on many human city-states in the south. However, with the death of the first Harpy Queen Firanya, her bickering daughters established their own flocks, splitting the once unified Queendom into petty squabbling.

Since then, many have tried to reestablish the once great realm but it was the flock of Ayara that has unified us for the final time against the now weakened Kingdom of Birzartanšes. Only as we unified under the true heir of Firanya could the flocks work together and establish dominance over the Harpy Hills once again.

description.text:
Due to the fractured nature of the flocks, separate cultures arose among the harpies who tried to claim the Queendom. As Mišqa reunited the flocks in 1342, she invited the Matriarchs to become advisors, diplomats and generals in her new order to both appease her new subjects and to use each flock’s strength to their best advantage.

With this, the Council of Matriarchs was established, a congregation of the wisest and strongest harpies who would be entrusted in the administration of the newly reclaimed lands.

description.text:
The Ištara Swoop is a special technique used by the Ayaralleni to utilise the cliffs and valleys of the Harpy Hills to descend on their enemies below, shattering formations and crushing morale. It was first utilised by Ayarallen during their clash with the state of Varamhar, where they issued a false retreat into a nearby valley to lure the pursuing eager soldiers into a narrow point.

Once the human army was at the end of the valley, harpy reinforcements appeared from atop the ledges of the canyon and swooped down with talons at the front, slaughtering many of the soldiers there. This one-sided battle deterred many future conquerors from travelling through the Harpy Hills unprepared, as one never knows when they'll be attacked from all fronts.

description.text:
While first seen as saviours to the Bulwari people, living under sun elf rule proved to be unlike the freedom the Bulwari people yearned for, and multiple restrictions were set in place from the people first seen as heroes. The Harpy method of governance, meanwhile, was a very loose concept and hardly impacted the Bulwari. Harpies did not impose significant taxes nor did they install governors.

Instead they preferred taking some of the men for mates and leaving those exchange villages as functionally independent with their own elected leaders, businesses and customs. These villages were free to continue practising their religion of choice.

description.text:
Long have harpies been stigmatised and reduced to being seen as barbaric man-snatchers by both elves and humans. While there may have been a grain of truth in this, we cannot tolerate this reputation any longer. We shall strive to correct our previous grievances and present our new Queendom in a new light.

Harpy emissaries trained in the arts of negotiation and clothed in the finest silks shall be sent to dazzle the various courts with the presence of the most charming diplomats. In time, our emissaries shall reach every corner of the world and bring the greater the respect our Queendom deserves.

description.text:
Inspired by the Gelkar weavers, many harpies have developed a unique form of art called feather tapestries. Skilled artisans meticulously weave together vibrant and colourful feathers of both rare birds from northern Bulwar and harpies to create intricate tapestries that depict mythological stories, historical events, and scenes from everyday life. Often used to educate young harpies and impress foreign dignitaries, they offered a tactile experience of Firanya’s legacy.

These feather tapestries would eventually become a cultural pillar of Harpylen and serve as a way to preserve the cultural heritage of each flock individually, depicting their unique cultures they had developed along with the mixes of elven and human ideas as they further got integrated in Harpyleni society.

description.text:
Our traditional roosts on the highest peaks of the Harpy Hills have long been the centres of our flock’s populations, where the old have settled and where the young took their first flights. Now, as our queendom expands and riches grow, new roosts may join the old.

Each one with grander constructions built by both our harpies and their mates. Atop every mountain harbours the potential for its own settlement, with grand markets and dwellings reaching towards the sky as our great civilisation grows to new heights.

description.text: Harpylen; a title given only to the land ruled by a true Queen of all Harpies. First realized by Firanya herself, this title is the dream of all who call themselves Firanya’s children. Many have claimed the title, although few have had any degree of legitimacy. The second Queendom was established by the flock Šumiryalen, and was only felled by the bronze dragon Aakhet himself. The third - an alliance between the Hytiranyalen and Lysinyalen flocks - firmly halted Akalšesi expansion into our hills. This third and most recent queendom fell beneath the Phoenix Legions of Jaher and his general Amarien. Ours is the fourth, and there will be no fifth.

description.text: Since time immemorial, harpies and their queendoms have been known for complex and conflict-averse foreign policy. The tributary arrangement extracted by Ayarallen from the remnants of Dartaxâgerdim in 1449 persisted more or less unchanged for centuries, despite continual instability across Bulwar, while the fourth Harpylen, which emerged as a nominal ally of the Jadd Empire before accepting the Divine Herald as the recognised overlord of Bulwar, retained extraordinary autonomy compared to other vassal polities of the period. Harpylen’s position at a crossroad of the Serpentspine, the Deepwoods, the Forbidden Plains and Bulwar made careful management of border tensions vital, but beyond this, the matriarchs of Harpylen fostered an institutional gravitas. By the end of the eighteenth century, the figure of the Harpylen diplomat was familiar enough to appear in novels from Anbenncóst to Feiten - they were stately, immensely well-informed, playing a complex and unclear game, and by the denouement very often vindicated.

description.text: The rivalry between Hytiranyalen and Ayarallen, sometimes fabled to stretch back to the daughters of Firanya herself, was contorted into a different shape as Ayarallen took the helm of a fourth Harpylen. Even Ayarallen could no longer deny the position and prominence of this ancient flock, famed above all for their "Odd Hunt", a practice dating back to the period of harpy history typified by seasonal raiding. A harpy on the Odd Hunt sought out any and all knowledge or information they could find; sourcing rare books, ferreting out technological blueprints or even kidnapping intellectuals for installation in their roosts. Under the fourth Harpylen, this practice took its recognisable modern form, a highly organised system of student exchanges and residencies predominantly conducted with the Overclan and the Jadd Empire. The Harpylen government benefited greatly from this exchange, most notably through the spread and popularisation of artificery from Drolakand and Aqatbar.

description.text: All harpies kneel to the Queen of Harpylen, this much is fact. Even those from far distant flocks recognize the position of the Queen, her title holds so much gravitas. The centralization of Harpylen was spearheaded by Ištara II Ayarato, promising autonomy and privileges to the other flocks in return for their support for various local administrative and institutional reforms within their lands. Of course, these concessions could be revoked if needed, and often were when the death of Matriarchs triggered the traditional instant dissolution of local government institutions, causing massive chaos for day to day administration. Tax exemptions and semi-autonomous trade allowances, as well as awarding prestigious, yet reasonable positions in the state hierarchy of Harpylen, were enough to convince most to allow the Ayarato administrators access to their lands and regional governments. With this, Harpylen evolved from a figure-driven empire of Harpies that would disintegrate at the first sign of challenge or death of a major Queen, to a modern state able to withstand and evolve with an ever-changing political and economic landscape.

description.text: Our hills lie at a crossroads of many important trade routes in and out of the Centaur Plains. We are the final stop between the Plains and both Southern Cannor and the Fey Woods, and we are able to exploit our position along these routes with extreme efficiency. Some of these trade routes are truly ancient, and our connection with the peoples of these lands has been tied into our existence since time immemorial. Our lands are filled with the coin of all corners of the world, and a great many riches have flown through our roosts and markets.

description.text: While the Harpylen state adopted the Jadd as its official religion upon its recognition of the sovereignty of the Divine-Herald over Bulwar, those within the Queendom maintained unparalleled and unprecedented freedoms in both cultural and religious practices. From the harpies of Lake Firanya, holdout followers of The Hunt and it’s practices, to Hytiranyalen, who practiced a kaleidoscope of different faiths as diverse as the books within their libraries, to the humans of Gelkalis and Garlas-Kel, followers of the New and Old Cults respectively, there was no real top-down enforcement of faith within the lands of the Queen. Harpyleni roosts were a metropolis of peoples: followers of Irdaeos from the plains, Fey cultists from the woods, elves and Half-elves from all corners of Cannor and Bulwar. By the eighteenth century, the roosts of Harpylen were extraordinarily religiously diverse and a popular haven for religious minorities fleeing persecution elsewhere - most notably Sun Cultists, Cannorian Pantheists and even elves still following the Forebears.

description.text: While Harpylen undoubtedly profited from the rich trade between the Plains and their trade partners in Cannor and the Fey Woods, the Harpy Hills were not without riches to call their own, boasting vast mineral wealth. While Harpylen remained poor in lumber and in fields with which to practice agriculture, it was able to tap enormous veins of metal which either remained or became vital to artificery and industrial development. Iron, Copper, Tin, Zinc, Aluminium and more all flowed from innumerable mines dotting the countryside. In comparison with the older Matriarchies, which were disconnected and thus unable to truly exploit the Hills’ mineral wealth, the fourth Harpylen had no such issue. Rich reserves, combined with robust Harpy infrastructure and transport, formed the backbone of the Harpyleni economy in the 17th and 18th centuries, allowing Harpylen to import grain and lumber in enormous quantities from the Overclan and the Jadd Empire.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you only want continuous wars and do not want to manage vassal loyalty, diplomacy, or construction requirements.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Manage vassals and nests first, integrate Bulwar through diplomacy, cultural acceptance, and conquest in the middle game, then meet the Queendom gate and form Harpylen.
player_overview.overview: You begin Ayarallen with two Harpy vassals, but they do not yet truly recognise one queen. Stabilise the tribes, expand the nests, and use marriage, vassals, and diplomacy to connect the hills and Suran Valley into a multi-peoples state. You must teach former raiders to govern cities while balancing queenly authority against local cultures; after the prequel, the country forms Harpylen and opens a longer Queendom campaign.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy vassal politics, inclusive state-building, and a prequel that leads into a long formable-country campaign.
signature_features: Nanšalen and Hytiranyalen begin as vassals, with integration shaped by relations, loyalty, and territorial arrangements.
Nest construction and Bulwari city management turn flying tribes into a settled multi-peoples country.
After gaining the early Queendom Claim power bar, the finale forms Harpylen and switches to an independent mission tree.
player_overview.tagline: Use Harpy nests, kinship, and diplomacy to bring Bulwar's peoples into the Fourth Queendom.

reasons: Two opening vassals make tribal politics actionable from the first day.
Nest construction, cultural coexistence, and diplomatic de-monsterisation give expansion a governance theme.
The F27 finale naturally hands into F98 for a complete Harpy Queendom campaign.
warnings: F27 and F98 are separate mission trees; F27 missions are not expected to remain visible after formation.
A vassal's extra territory and loyalty can change the early integration result.
The full F27→F98 campaign is much longer than F27's 20 missions alone.

values.rationale: The route actively eases old human-goblin grievances, accepts multiple cultures, respects local faiths, and advances de-monsterisation; queenly authority and vassal expansion reduce restraint but do not negate the inclusive direction.
